> I think the only time CSP is not important is when you have static HTML. 

Not entirely true, but it is covered by another requirement - from an embedding point of view, it must always be disabled because, lacking CSP/XFO, for example, error messages give an option to bypass CSP rules in an HTML injection situation.

I don't have any good proposal at the moment for the requirement, but at the same time, it is clear that the current one can cause false positives in reports, for example, when required for a response that serves a jpg image.

---

One direction - we should ask for only responses that require content rendering from the browser.

Other direction, (that we have at the moment) to allow situations where serving non-renderable content does not need to contain the header field, then most likely it will be missing also for error messages from the same endpoint.
